ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a grave for {OTHER_nameDef}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A named or bonded animal has died, and its body still lies at home. The one who loved it wants it buried, not butchered.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: {OTHER_nameDef}'s body rests in a grave. Promised, {FOR_nameDef} digs one near the colony and carries the body into it.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is still lying out there. I'd like to bury {OTHER_objective} before anyone gets ideas about the meat.
Let me dig {OTHER_nameDef} a grave. It won't take long, and I'd rather do it myself.
[trigger:death] {OTHER_nameDef} died this morning. I want {OTHER_objective} in the ground, near home, not in the butcher's pile.
[rain] It's raining on {OTHER_nameDef}. Please, let me put {OTHER_objective} somewhere dry and deep.
[winter] The ground is hard, but {OTHER_nameDef} deserves a grave all the same.
[child] Can we bury {OTHER_nameDef}? Properly, with a grave, like people get?

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} waited at the door for me every day. The least I can do is give {OTHER_objective} a place to rest.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had a good life with us. Let's give {OTHER_objective} a good spot in the sun to finish it.

gloomy.li: Everything out here ends in the dirt. At least let {OTHER_nameDef}'s be a grave.

cold.li: A body left lying draws scavengers. {OTHER_nameDef} gets buried, and I'll do it.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is in the ground now, near home. Thank you.
I dug it deep. Nothing will bother {OTHER_objective} there.

warm.li: I told {OTHER_nameDef} goodbye properly. Thank you for the time to do it.

cheerful.li: It's a nice spot. {OTHER_nameDef} would have liked it.

gloomy.li: At least {OTHER_nameDef} has a grave. Most things out here don't get one.

plain.li: So nobody had time to bury {OTHER_nameDef}.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} deserved better than to lie out there.

blunt.li: I'll remember who couldn't spare an hour.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a field of {SUBJECT}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Spring, and someone misses a crop from home: a fruit, a vegetable or a flower the colony could sow now and doesn't grow anywhere.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Six plants of {SUBJECT} are sown in the colony's fields or growers. Promised, a small field of it is laid out beside the others.

plain.li: We grew {SUBJECT} back home. I'd give a lot to see a row of it out there.
It's planting time, and nobody's sowing {SUBJECT}. Could we spare a corner of the field?
[spring] Every spring at home we put in {SUBJECT}. It doesn't feel like spring without it.
[child] Can we grow {SUBJECT}? I've never seen it growing, only heard about it.
[old] My mother grew {SUBJECT}. I'd like to see it come up once more.

warm.li: Just a small patch of {SUBJECT}. I'd tend it myself, every morning.

blunt.li: Sow some {SUBJECT}. The ground's ready and so am I.

cheerful.li: Picture a whole row of {SUBJECT}, right out there by the others.

gloomy.li: Nothing here tastes like home. A field of {SUBJECT} might help, a little.

cold.li: We have the seed and the season for {SUBJECT}. Not sowing it is a waste.

plain.li: It's coming up. Real {SUBJECT}, here, in our ground.
I walked the rows this morning before anyone else was up.

warm.li: It smells like home out there now. Thank you.

cheerful.li: Come and look at the {SUBJECT}! Little green shoots, every one of them.

gloomy.li: I didn't think I'd see it again.

cold.li: A sensible use of the season.

plain.li: Maybe next spring.

gloomy.li: Home is a long way off, and getting further.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: something green in winter
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Fall or winter in a land with a real winter, and the colony has power and could build a sun lamp. A grower, or someone who has gone without fresh food, wants a sun lamp over an indoor field.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: A sun lamp is lit over six or more roofed cells of a growing zone or hydroponics. Promised, one is planned in the middle of an indoor field that has none.

plain.li: The fields will be under snow soon. With a sun lamp indoors we could keep something green growing.
I haven't had anything fresh in days. A lamp over an indoor field would see us through the cold.
[trigger:scurvy] My gums are bleeding. We need greens growing indoors before the winter gets worse.
[winter] Everything outside is dead or frozen. Let's grow something under a lamp.

warm.li: A little green in the dark months would do everyone good, not just me.

blunt.li: Build a sun lamp over a field indoors. We'll want the food.

cheerful.li: Strawberries in winter, or at least potatoes. A sun lamp would do it.

gloomy.li: It's going to be a long, grey winter. Something growing would help.

cold.li: We have the power and the knowledge. Indoor crops through the winter are simply sense.

plain.li: There's green under the lamp, and snow outside. That's how it should be.
I went and stood under it for a minute. It's warm, like summer.

warm.li: Everyone will eat better this winter. Thank you.

cheerful.li: It's like a little summer in there!

gloomy.li: At least something will grow this winter.

cold.li: The lamp is lit and the field is sown. Well done.

plain.li: So it'll be meat and more meat until spring.

gloomy.li: A long winter, and nothing green in it.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a lamp at the {SUBJECT}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Someone has been working at a bench, or researching, in the dark. They want a lamp where they work.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: A lamp's light reaches the {SUBJECT}'s work spot, day or night. Promised, {THING} is planned beside it.

plain.li: I was at the {SUBJECT} in the dark again last night. I can barely see my own hands.
A lamp by the {SUBJECT}, that's all. I keep squinting until my head aches.
[night] It's too dark to work at the {SUBJECT}, and the work doesn't wait for morning.
[old] My eyes aren't what they were. I need light at the {SUBJECT}.

warm.li: Whoever works the {SUBJECT} after me will thank you for a lamp there too.

blunt.li: Put a lamp by the {SUBJECT}. I'm working blind.

cheerful.li: Give me a lamp at the {SUBJECT} and I'll work twice as well, I promise.

gloomy.li: One of these days I'll ruin something at the {SUBJECT} because I can't see it.

cold.li: Work done in the dark is work done badly. A lamp at the {SUBJECT} pays for itself.

plain.li: I can see the grain of the work now. Thank you.
Light at the bench. Small thing, big difference.

warm.li: My eyes thank you, and so do I.

cheerful.li: It's bright as noon in here now.

gloomy.li: At least I won't go blind at it.

plain.li: Back to squinting, then.

blunt.li: Don't complain about my work if you won't light it.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a roof over the way to the table
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: In a wet land, someone came in soaked to the table or to bed. They want the open steps between their bed and the table roofed.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: All {TARGET} open steps of the way from {FOR_nameDef}'s bed to the table are under a roof. Promised, they're marked for roofing, and the colony's builders put the roof up.

plain.li: I came to supper soaked through again. It's only a few steps, but they're open to the sky.
Could we roof the way from the bedrooms to the table? I'm tired of eating wet.
[trigger:soaked] Look at me, dripping on the floor. A roof over that bit of path would end it.
[rain] It's raining again, and there's no getting to the table dry.

warm.li: Everyone gets wet on that path, not just me. A roof would spare us all.

blunt.li: Roof the path to the table. I'm sick of being wet.

cheerful.li: I'd love to get to breakfast without a bath on the way!

gloomy.li: Wet to bed, wet to breakfast. That's the whole season.

cold.li: A few cells of roof would save hours of drying clothes. The sums are easy.

plain.li: Dry all the way to the table. I didn't know I'd missed it so much.
I listened to the rain on the new roof on the way to supper.

warm.li: Thank you, from all of us who walk that way.

cheerful.li: Rain all day and not a drop on me.

gloomy.li: One less thing to be miserable about.

plain.li: Wet it is, then.

gloomy.li: I'll be soaked again by supper.
